title: Lettuce Salad with Cheese, Tomato and/or Carrot, No Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Lettuce salad is a mix of fresh leafy lettuce, cheese, tomato and carrot, with optional additional vegetables. No dressing is used to preserve the natural flavors of the ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Leafy lettuce is high in water content and helps maintain hydration.
Cheese can be soft (feta, mozzarella) or hard (cheddar, parmesan).
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that is enhanced by cooking but remains beneficial raw.
Carrot is one of the most accessible sources of beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
The absence of dressing makes the salad low‑calorie and allows better control of fat intake.

items.title: Vision support
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrot and vitamin A help maintain healthy eyesight.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomato and vitamin C from lettuce combat free radicals.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium from cheese and vitamin K from lettuce contribute to bone strength.

items.title: Hydration and low calories
items.content: High water content and no dressing make the dish light and supportive of fluid balance.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Lettuce and carrot provide fiber that supports digestive regularity.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Non‑organic vegetables may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: High‑salt cheeses can increase sodium intake; choose low‑salt or reduced‑fat options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad immediately after chopping to keep it crisp. Optional additions include nuts, seeds, or fresh herbs. A light squeeze of lemon juice can be added if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ingredients separately in the refrigerator: lettuce in an airtight container with a paper towel, cheese wrapped in film, and cut vegetables in a sealed dish. Assembled salad is best consumed within 2‑3 hours.
